title: Milk, nonfat, fluid, with added vitamin A and vitamin D

content.title: About
content.content: Nonfat milk is whole cow’s milk from which almost all fat has been removed (usually less than 0.5%). Vitamin A and vitamin D are added to compensate for the loss of these nutrients during fat removal. The product is pasteurized, sealed in airtight containers, and kept refrigerated.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nonfat milk contains almost the same amount of protein, calcium, and lactose as whole milk.
Vitamin A supports vision, while vitamin D aids calcium absorption.
In the US and Canada it is called “skim milk”; in Russia it is often labeled “milk 0%”.
Nonfat milk generally has a longer shelf‑life after pasteurization than whole milk.
In many countries the addition of vitamins A and D to nonfat milk is mandated by law.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and teeth health and is essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Makes it suitable for calorie‑controlled and low‑fat diets.

items.title: Vitamin A
items.content: Important for eye health, immune function, and skin integrity.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Enhances absorption of calcium and phosphorus, promoting strong bones.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Milk protein provides all essential amino acids needed for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People lacking lactase may experience bloating, diarrhea, and discomfort after consuming milk.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions can range from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Vitamin A excess
items.content: Too much vitamin A can be toxic, especially when combined with other sources.

items.title: Vitamin D excess
items.content: Excessive intake may lead to hypercalcemia.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink it plain, add to cereals, smoothies, coffee, baking recipes, or sauces. The added vitamins do not alter the taste but increase the nutritional value.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Do not freeze, as it can affect protein structure.
